items.quote: shall remaine like a pure, cleare, incorruptible and fixed Essence in a serene resplendent Chrystalin Earth
items.note: What in the Elements does not fear the Fire of Heaven will remain as a fixed, incorruptible Essence in a crystalline Earth.

items.quote: when God shall change all things by making them new according to his will, and shall make them all like Christall
items.note: At God's renewal of all things they become like crystal and the motions of the Supernaturall Nature abide in them without corruption.

items.quote: would bestow some part of their wealth upon men piously and consciensciously learned and skilfull in Chymistry
items.note: Croll wishes the Great Ones would pay pious, skilled chymists, each set his task.

items.quote: to find out one out of those Three Families of Nature
items.note: The text names the Three Families and lists them at once: Animalls, Vegetables, and Mineralls, the things in which all Physick is founded.

items.quote: separating them by Fire into their Three First (things.)
items.note: The work: fetching the choicest Physicall Mysteries out of the three families by separating them by Fire into their Three First.

items.quote: All beauty, corporeal and incorporeall is nothing else but the splendor of the Divine countenance and Light set in created things
items.note: Beauty is defined as the Divine Light shining out through created things.

items.quote: For so much Light as a King hath in him, so much Majesty hath he.
items.note: A king's majesty is measured by the Light in him; the Latin Quantum Luminis, tantum Numinis follows.

items.quote: The Phylosophicall Conclave of any Prince furnished with such most precious and wholesome a Treasure
items.note: A prince's store of the separated preparations is named a Phylosophicall Conclave, compared with the riches of Pactolus.

items.quote: to contemplate the open riches of secret Nature
items.note: Nature is called secret; the Conclave would set its riches open to view.

items.quote: answering to the members of our body by an Harmonicall Anatomy
items.note: The vegetables are said to correspond to the members of the body; the correspondence is named an Anatomy.

items.quote: in their Three First (principles) with their garments put off; made naked and visible
items.note: The separated Three First are described as unclothed: the work is spoken of as stripping garments.

items.quote: the TRIUNE naked DIANA shining with so many colours of variety and alwayes with a Triple Form in every classis or distribution
items.note: The minerals and metals so separated are named a threefold naked Diana with a Triple Form in every class. Interpreted: Diana stands here as a figure for the three separated forms, since the text at once names those forms as hers.

items.quote: a most limpid or clear MERCURIAL, a most garnished SULPHUREAN or oyly, and a most bright pure SALINE form
items.note: The text spells out Diana's Triple Form: Mercurial (clear), Sulphurean (oily), Saline.

items.quote: who otherwise covereth her selfe from the dishonest looks of mortalls
items.note: Diana otherwise covers herself and does not come among men in this worldly scene with her veile.

items.quote: Francis the First King of France, the greatest Favorer of Phylosophers and learned men, intended to go about one of the Three, but was prevented by death.
items.note: Croll reports a king who meant to undertake one of the Three Families and died first.

items.quote: the sole fountaine being reserved to it selfe for its own uses, but by drawing forth spare streams
items.note: The source itself is kept reserved; only spare streams are drawn off for giving.

items.quote: to do good to God, with this Talent, in our poor neighbour and his members
items.note: The use of the gift is charity: an Almoner's duty to the poor neighbour.

items.quote: every good Gift upon amendment of Life is by asking, seeking, and knocking, to be obtained
items.note: Every good gift comes from the Father of Lights, to be got by asking, seeking and knocking after amendment of life.

items.quote: By the Light of God, secret and hidden things are revealed and made manifest.
items.note: Hidden things are revealed by God's Light.

items.name: Psal.; Prov.
items.note: Scripture places cited beside CH6.34.

items.quote: For this onely is the Kings high-way, not onely to come all the desired Secrets of Nature
items.note: The pious way is named the only King's highway, to the Secrets of Nature and to the workmaster of the universe. The name returns in CH6.48 (Rode or Kings Highway).

items.quote: by which ONE infinite OCEAN of all Divine GOODNES through Regeneration (alterity being swallowed up of unity)
items.note: Regeneration is used of the soul's return to God, where otherness is swallowed by unity; the same word is used of the medicine in CH6.38.

items.quote: There is no recovering or returning to what we have lost but by the Crosse and Death
items.note: The way back is only through Cross, Death, the Fire of Temptation and Tribulation.

items.quote: He that knows One knows All things
items.note: Knowledge of the One is knowledge of all.

items.quote: We cannot get the Victory and Crown of Patience without striving & fighting.
items.note: The crown comes after struggle; a Latin tag with illegible letters follows.

items.name: Eccl.; Levit.; Tob.; Prov
items.note: Scripture places cited beside CH6.35 (also Levit. 25. Tob. 12.13. Eccl. 2.5. Prov 17.3).

items.quote: to enter into the inner rooms of that supream Phylosophicall Oratory
items.note: The highest attainment is named an Oratory with inner rooms; Croll says he long desired to enter, in vain.

items.quote: not to the end that I might make Gold and Silver
items.note: Croll says his aim was not gold and silver but to find out the True Physick.

items.quote: though I cannot proceed further as yet, I comfort my selfe with the cogitation onely
items.note: Croll states he has not himself gone further; envy and fortune hindered him.

items.quote: God himselfe knoweth what, to whom, when and how is fit
items.note: God decides who receives what, and withholds what might hurt.

items.name: Num.; Psal.; Tob.
items.note: Scripture places cited beside CH6.36.

items.quote: was shewed to me as an eye-witnesse in my travells
items.note: Croll claims he saw and tasted it as an eye-witness at a great man's house, as attestation of the Truth.

items.quote: Which I forbear to English.
items.note: The Latin naming the house and its master is left untranslated by the English.

items.quote: cujuSmodi lENtis DenIque consueVerunt latitare tempOrum currIcVlis
items.note: The Latin has capitals set inside words (also in Cumprimis egregium Helioch Antharum bor EaLem). Several defensible readings: the capitals mark letters to be read apart (a covered name or number), or they are printing irregularities; the text does not say which.

items.quote: the greatest miracle of Nature wrought by Art
items.what: the greatest miracle of Nature wrought by Art
items.note: The thing he saw is set apart as Nature's greatest miracle done by Art.

items.quote: the various and manifold metamorphosis of the Inferior Astronomy made in the cold
items.note: The work's changes are called an Inferior Astronomy, done in the cold.

items.quote: the Moyst way of the Ancients not as yet intensly exalted to the eye of the Basilisk
items.what: the Moyst way of the Ancients
items.note: A named way of working, the Moist way, said not yet exalted to the eye of the Basilisk.

items.quote: that Latex or liquor
items.note: Latex is glossed as liquor.

items.quote: a man desperately sick and at the point of death was recovered
items.note: One drop of the liquor given to a dying man restored him to health in one night.

items.quote: in which as in a storehouse the dispersed vertues of all Celestiall and Terrestriall bodies were by a wonderfull artifice invisibly gathered together in an heap
items.note: The liquor holds the gathered virtues of all bodies; the whole world centred in it.

items.quote: For this Kingly medicine, and the Empresse of all other
items.what: this Kingly medicine, and the Empresse of all other
items.note: The liquor is named the Kingly medicine and Empress of medicines.

items.quote: for many diseases are a Divine innate punishment, for which there is no cure in Nature
items.note: Limit: diseases that are God's punishment have no natural cure.

items.quote: this whole new regenerate world is able by vertue of its Regeneration to renew the little old corruptible world Man
items.note: The medicine is called a new regenerate world, man the little old world (Microcosm) it renews.

items.quote: The Physophycall Basilisk like Lightning suddenly and unawares burneth up any imperfect mettall whatsoever
items.note: The Basilisk is named as the thing that consumes imperfect metal and suddenly produces a new form; its searching out is commended.

items.quote: There is no Physitian can cure death, but Christ.
items.note: The medicine's limit: death.

items.quote: they are restored to their True Health, which is aureity or goldness
items.note: For metals, True Health is said to be aureity or goldness.

items.quote: without a new motion of generation and corruption, by way of alteration onely, and remotion of accidents
items.note: Impure metals are cleansed by the spirit of the world and Heat of Sun and Moon, by alteration and removal of accidents.

items.quote: for mettals doe not differ in specie but onely in accidents
items.note: Metals differ only in accidents, not in kind.

items.quote: justly not to be made known (though it be truer then true) to our Vulgar sort
items.note: The secret is rightly kept from the Vulgar sort.

items.quote: because they never heard any thing in all their life of the Heat of the Sun and Moon
items.term: Heat of the Sun and Moon
items.note: The Heat of the Sun and Moon (also in CH6.39) is a phrase the ignorant do not know; it is used as an agent of the work, not plainly of weather.

items.quote: that the Element of EARTH should by the help of Mechanick Magick swim upon the water
items.note: A harder marvel set beside the first: Earth made to swim upon water by Mechanick Magick.

items.quote: for upon that account God provideth for the security of those that give themselves truly to the study of Phylosophy
items.note: Common disbelief in the Art is said to protect its true students.

items.name: Exod.; Job
items.note: Scripture places cited beside CH6.40.

items.quote: the four Monarchs of all diseases, the Epilepsie, Gout, Dropsie, Leprosie
items.note: The four Monarchs of diseases are named.

items.quote: proving in some of his works that God taught him the medicine
items.name: Paracelsus
items.note: Paracelsus is said to have cured the four by a wonderful Art, God having taught him the medicine.

items.quote: by Restoring or regenerating ones, which are known to very few
items.note: The restoring medicines are known to very few.

items.quote: as his Epitaph at Salisburg doth truly and sufficiently witnesse to posterity
items.note: Points to Paracelsus's epitaph at Salisburg as witness; also to some of his works.

items.quote: it is not the first but second birth that produceth it
items.note: The foundation of true physicians is produced by a second birth, not the first.

items.quote: are healed by this universall medicine, as a Carpenter that squareth all kind of timber
items.note: All diseases from corrupted humours are healed by the universall medicine, save at life's appointed term or a disease inflicted by God.

items.quote: But no man, as hath been said, can make use of this peculiar and celestiall Gift
items.note: Refers back to an earlier statement that only those God gives it to can use the Gift.

items.quote: who onely both inlightneth the obscurity, and darkneth the clearnesse of these mysteries
items.note: God alone makes the mysteries clear or dark, so none understands the plainest things unless enlightened.

items.quote: between the Artist and God the first cause, there ought to be an agreement without contrariety
items.name: Lullius
items.note: Lullius concluded the first mover must move the Artist's soul to understanding.

items.quote: that he may open to him what is hid in the magistery of this Art
items.note: What is hidden in the magistery is opened by God to the Artist.

items.quote: answerable to the unworthy publishing of this most True Phylosophicall Art
items.note: Two public philosophers of Croll's time came to a doleful end matching their unworthy publishing of the Art.

items.quote: against those most horrid Anathema's of Phylosophers
items.name: Phylosophers
items.note: The philosophers' curses against misuse of the Gifts are invoked.

items.quote: their cheating Impostures of the first Hapocraticall silence
items.note: A named silence the offenders broke or counterfeited by turns to cloak the matter.

items.quote: every man according to his dexterity which the sydereall spirit causeth and exciteth is the forger of his own fortune
items.note: Each man forges his own fortune by the dexterity the sydereall spirit stirs.

items.quote: The originall of the Philosophicall Magistery.
items.what: The originall of the Philosophicall Magistery
items.note: The note heads the passage as the origin of the Magistery.

items.quote: when it is only but imaginary
items.note: Many who boast of clear knowledge of it have only imagined it, and so hinder themselves.

items.quote: the children of Hermes who first found out the science
items.note: The ancient philosophers are named children of Hermes and finders of the science.

items.quote: to have it indeed without the witnesse of a sottish ignorant multitude, then seeme or be supposed onely to have it
items.note: They preferred to have it unseen by the multitude rather than to seem to have it.

items.quote: these private not publick Secretaries of Nature
items.what: private not publick Secretaries of Nature
items.note: The ancient adepts are named private Secretaries of Nature, rejoicing in Quiet Silence.

items.quote: In the first age of the world God made it known by the Light of Nature.
items.note: It was made known in the first age by the Light of Nature.

items.quote: This is Phylosophy Adept, which Paracelsus in the Tincture of Physicks explaineth them to be Long Life and free from all infirmity
items.name: Paracelsus
items.note: Phylosophy Adept is named and, after Paracelsus's Tincture of Physicks, said to be long life free of infirmity and honest support.

items.quote: a wonderfull and most abstruse comprehending of all the vertues of the whole Creation flowing and running together in one certaine masse
items.note: The happiness is reached only by gathering all virtues of creation into one mass, in this Rode or Kings Highway.

items.quote: being by great help of ingenuity and Art like the lesser world heaped up together and concentred into one masse
items.note: The spiritual virtues are heaped and concentred into one mass by Art, like the lesser world.

items.quote: a kind of sweetest and admirable illustration of the Mind
items.note: Those who have it gain illumination of mind, knowledge of natural things and heavenly secrets, and plenty.

items.quote: The defect of Nature must be supplyed by the industry of Art
items.note: Art supplies what Nature lacks, Nature tending toward perfection.

items.quote: Prov. 3.16.
items.name: Prov.
items.note: Scripture place cited beside CH6.49.

items.quote: though they have been altogether dumb in keeping close the secret of the Art by a constant Taciturnity
items.note: The Hermetic philosophers kept the secret closed by constant silence, for fear of danger.

items.quote: Of which the Phylosophers our predecessors that have been train'd up in Hermes school
items.name: Phylosophers our predecessors that have been train'd up in Hermes school
items.note: These philosophers are given the Reason that follows on what the Medicine is.

items.quote: our Balsom, that is, the spirit or celestiall▪ not visible vapour of life
items.note: Balsom is defined as the celestial, invisible vapour of life, which the Medicine quickens.

items.quote: the Fift Essence compounded of the four Elements
items.note: The Medicine is named the Fifth Essence, all Elements in it bound with a golden chaine without contrariety.

items.quote: like as in Lightning and the eye of a Basilisk
items.note: The subtle working on diseases and metals is likened to Lightning and the Basilisk's eye, as in CH6.38 and N274.

items.quote: as the Heaven is incorruptible in respect of the four Elements
items.note: The Medicine stands to the four qualities of the body as Heaven to the four Elements.

items.quote: They durst not under paine of Anathema to speak of it, but in a picture of Aenigmaticall words
items.note: They spoke of it only in enigmatic words, the Master of Nature not giving leave.

items.quote: for the Naturall life is nothing else but the actings of the Elements
items.note: Natural life is defined as the acting of the Elements.

items.name: Prov.
items.note: Scripture place cited beside CH6.50.
